statement: What is the remainder when 2 to the power 100 is divided by 7?

choices.misconception: I worked out the last digit of the power first and then divided that by 7.
I found the cycle 2, 4, 1 but used a remainder of 2 where dividing 100 by 3 gives 1.
I assumed the cycle had length 4 out of habit from last-digit questions, so I landed in the wrong place.
I treated 100 as a multiple of the cycle length 3 and took the value at the end of the cycle.

hints: Work out the first few remainders and watch for a repeat.
Powers of a fixed base leave remainders that cycle. Find the cycle length, divide the exponent by it, and read off the position the remainder points to.
The remainders run 2, 4, 1 and then repeat, so the cycle has length 3. Since 100 = 33 x 3 + 1, the answer sits at the first position.

solutions.reliable: Powers of 2 leave remainders 2, 4, 1 on division by 7, repeating with period 3. Because 100 leaves remainder 1 on division by 3, the hundredth power sits at the first position in the cycle. The transferable idea: modular arithmetic turns an unreachable exponent into a remainder on a tiny cycle length.
solutions.elegant: 2 cubed is 8, which is one more than 7, so 2 to the 99 behaves like 1 and only one factor of 2 is left over.

whyOnTest: Exponents far beyond any calculator are standard in the 4-point block, and the cycle length is what a student must find rather than recall.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
